content: Windows uses mandatory file locking (unlike POSIX): any process holding a file handle open (antivirus/Defender real-time scan, Search indexer, another Node process, a stray watcher) blocks fs.rename with EPERM, often in a sub-50ms window right after the temp file is written. npm's own tooling hits this: write-file-atomic and graceful-fs's Windows rename-retry only fires when the destination does NOT already exist -- retry is skipped for the common overwrite-existing-file case, requiring an explicit retry-with-backoff wrapper (e.g. promise-retry on EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, Windows-only). Practical mitigations: retry loop (3-5 attempts, exponential backoff) around rename specifically on win32, and recommend users add antivirus exclusions for the project's config directories.
